title: Bulk-boundary correspondence of (1+1)D symmetric gapped phases
authors: Yizhou Ma, Gen Yue, Tian Lan
abstract: We develop an operator-algebraic framework for boundary conditions and bulk-boundary correspondence in one-dimensional gapped phases with categorical symmetry. Working directly in the thermodynamic limit, we construct half-infinite fusion spin chains and commuting-projector boundary Hamiltonians from a unitary fusion category $\mathcal{C}$, an indecomposable semisimple right $\mathcal{C}$-module category $\mathcal{M}$, a Q-system $Q\in\mathcal{C}$ specifying the bulk phase, and a right $Q$-module $K\in\mathcal{M}_{Q}$, regarded as an object of $\mathcal{M}_{Q}^{\mathrm{op}}$, specifying the boundary. We prove that these Hamiltonians have unique ground states and that the resulting realization functor $\mathcal{M}_{Q}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{BCond}$ is an equivalence, so simple boundary conditions are classified by simple objects of $\mathcal{M}_{Q}$ and general boundary conditions by their finite direct sums. We also give a microscopic formulation of the boundary symmetry topological field theory using DHR bimodules of the boundary quasi-local algebra. For a half-infinite fusion spin chain, the boundary DHR category is monoidally equivalent to $(\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\vee})^{\mathrm{rev}}$, and the canonical action of the bulk DHR category on it agrees with the categorical action of $Z_1(\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{rev}})$. Finally, we identify the action of the boundary DHR category on boundary conditions with the categorical action of $(\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\vee})^{\mathrm{rev}}$ on $\mathcal{M}_{Q}^{\mathrm{op}}$. This yields a one-dimensional bulk-boundary correspondence: the enriched monoidal category describing the bulk is the enriched center of the enriched category describing the boundary.
summary: This theoretical work establishes a comprehensive bulk-boundary correspondence for one-dimensional gapped quantum phases with generalized symmetries. By employing operator algebras and advanced category theory, the authors rigorously prove that the bulk topological order can be mathematically derived from the structure of the boundary physics via the enriched center construction. This provides a powerful classification tool for understanding how edge states are dictated by the bulk material properties.
main_problem: The paper develops a rigorous operator-algebraic framework to establish the bulk-boundary correspondence for $(1+1)$D gapped quantum phases possessing categorical symmetry.
main_result: It proves that the enriched monoidal category describing the bulk topological structure is equivalent to the enriched center of the category describing the boundary physics. This provides a complete mathematical classification linking bulk and edge properties.
method: The methodology relies on working in the thermodynamic limit using $C^*$-algebras, constructing Hamiltonians via commuting-projector interactions, and employing advanced tools from enriched category theory (DHR bimodules, centers of categories).
model_or_system: The focus is on one-dimensional gapped quantum spin chains exhibiting categorical symmetry. The analysis uses abstract mathematical structures like unitary fusion categories ($\mathcal{C}$) and module categories ($\mathcal{M}$), rather than a single concrete Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Ground states of constructed Hamiltonians, the boundary DHR category, and the bulk/boundary topological field theories (SymTFTs).
important_parameters: The system is analyzed in the thermodynamic limit; symmetry structure is governed by the fusion category $\mathcal{C}$.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the existence of a unitary fusion category and an indecomposable semisimple right module category, allowing for the construction of quasi-local algebras.
figures_summary: Figure 6 summarizes the complete description of 1D symmetric gapped phases, relating four components: bulk SymTFT, boundary SymTFT, the category of boundary conditions ($	ext{BCond}$), and the underlying algebraic structures.
paper_structure: The paper builds from general concepts in infinite lattice algebras (AF algebras) to specific constructions for fusion spin chains. It then systematically establishes equivalences between operator-algebraic descriptions of boundary physics (via DHR categories) and abstract categorical definitions, culminating in the central theorem relating bulk structure to the center of the boundary structure.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical machinery developed—connecting algebraic structures like centers of enriched categories to physical observables—provides a powerful, general tool for classifying topological phases beyond simple symmetry groups, which is highly relevant for understanding correlated electron systems.
